items.title: I mastered my role. Now I have no idea what comes next.
items.pt:
I didn't end up where I planned.


I came into tech wanting to write code. I'd been self-teaching JavaScript, building small things, convinced I was headed for a developer role. Then I landed in integration engineering, configuring enterprise platforms, building workflows sending data to Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Adobe Campaign, WhatsApp Business API and then something unexpected happened.


  
  
  I loved it.


Not in a "this is fine" way. In a genuinely engaged, staying late because I want

items.title: How Does Distribution Shift Shape Pretraining Gains in Neural PDE Surrogates?
items.pt: Pretraining a neural PDE surrogate can reduce the amount of new CFD data needed when geometry or modeled physics changes. items.title: Quantifying Overclaiming Propensity in Frontier LLM Agents
items.pt: Frontier coding agents are increasingly trusted to work autonomously for long periods, yet an agent's final response is often the only account of that work a user sees. We quantify the propensity of frontier agents to \emph{overclaim} task completion, a misrepresentation that can mislead the user. An agent overclaims when its final response contradicts information in its context. This definition requires no inference about intent and is independent of task success. items.title: An Empirical Study of Harness Design for Coding Agents
items.pt: Coding harnesses shape how autonomous coding agents translate model capabilities into long-horizon software-engineering performance, yet existing work typically evaluates harnesses as monolithic systems, leaving the effectiveness of individual components unclear. items.title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
items.pt: Generative models are increasingly used to solve scientific inverse problems, but existing evaluations still focus primarily on whether a method can produce a single plausible reconstruction. This is insufficient for ill-posed problems, where multiple solutions may be consistent with the same sparse or noisy observations.
